content: Cabozantinib metabolism is affected by hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is required, reduce the cabozantinib dose by 40 mg/day (Cometriq) or 20 mg/day (Cabometyx). Resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Darunavir increases calcitriol levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases capivasertib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. Darunavir increases ceritinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ceritinib increases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Chloramphenicol increases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine increases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir increases cobicistat levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases colchicine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid colchicine use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If coadministration is necessary, reduce colchicine dose or frequency as recommended in prescribing information. Colchicine use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Darunavir decreases conjugated estrogens levels or effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases copanlisib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. Darunavir increases dabrafenib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases daridorexant levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases diazepam levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Use alternatives if available. Darunavir increases dofetilide levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Increased toxicity risk, including QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. Use alternatives if available. Darunavir increases edoxaban levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, decrease the dose to 30 mg PO once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended. Efavirenz decreases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with efavirenz may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance to darunavir. Darunavir increases elacestrant levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases elbasvir/grazoprevir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir decreases the effects of elivaldogene autotemcel. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Patients should not take antiretroviral medications for at least one month before initiating medications for stem cell mobilization, during the medication period, and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Darunavir increases encorafenib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose (e.g., reduce from 450 mg/day to 150 mg/day). After discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives, resume the previous encorafenib dose. Darunavir increases entrectinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate. Resume the previous entrectinib dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. Darunavir increases enzalutamide levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Enzalutamide decreases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases erdafitinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider decreasing the dose accordingly. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the erdafitinib dose in the absence of any drug-related toxicities. Darunavir increases ergoloid mesylates levels by decreasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir increases ergotamine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for serious and/or life-threatening reactions such as acute ergot toxicity, characterized by peripheral vasospasm and ischemia of the extremities and other tissues. Darunavir increases erythromycin base levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir increases erythromycin stearate levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases everolimus levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases fedratinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, decrease the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase the fedratinib dose to 300 mg/day for 2 weeks, then 400 mg/day thereafter as tolerated. Darunavir increases felbamate levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir decreases fexinidazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole increases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4. Coadministration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Darunavir increases flutamide levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases fluticasone intranasal levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects; monitor for signs/symptoms of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type signs/symptoms. Darunavir increases gilteritinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternatives to any strong CYP3A4 inhibitor when coadministered with gilteritinib. If such a combination cannot be avoided, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. Interrupt and reduce gilteritinib dosage in patients with serious or life-threatening toxicity. Darunavir increases glasdegib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative therapies that are not strong CYP3A inhibitors or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. Darunavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by decreasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir with darunavir (P-gp and a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor). Darunavir increases ibrutinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid concomitant use of ibrutinib and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued. Darunavir increases idelalisib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity; follow recommendations for dosage modifications if adverse reactions occur. Idelalisib increases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Darunavir increases infigratinib (DSC) levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases ivosidenib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. If coadministration of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg qDay. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose (after at least 5 half-lives of the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor) to the recommended dose of 500 mg qDay. Ivosidenib decreases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of therapeutic effect of these drugs. Ketoconazole and darunavir mutually increase each other's effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole are not available when coadministered with darunavir. Darunavir increases larotrectinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases lefamulin levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Darunavir increases lemborexant levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. Darunavir increases leniolisib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Levo-ketoconazole and darunavir mutually increase each other's effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole are not available when coadministered with darunavir. Darunavir, levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate: Significant changes (increase or decrease) can occur in estrogen plasma levels. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced. Use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. Lopinavir decreases darunavir levels by increasing metabolism. Lopinavir increases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases lorlatinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministering lorlatinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. If the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, increase to the previous lorlatinib dose (after 3 plasma half-lives of the strong CYP3A inhibitor). Lorlatinib decreases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Darunavir, lovotibeglogene autotemcel: Discontinue antiretrovirals (ARTs) at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting ARTs may require a longer duration of discontinuation for elimination. ARTs may interfere with lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing. Darunavir increases lurbinectedin levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After strong CYP3A inhibitor discontinued for 5 half-lives, increase lurbinectedin to dose used before coadministration. Darunavir increases macitentan levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
